ideas.title: I thought a symbol legend would help. The test said no.
ideas.angle: Published negative result across 8 vision models. Priming the detector with a floor-plan symbol legend did not help — a 15,000-char text legend actively HURT Gemini. The real miss is placement and topology, which no detector prompt addresses. Owners read integrity; hiring managers read experimental discipline.
ideas.proof_plan: Ground truth: 43 fixtures across 15 types, one plan, from a verified coordinate file. Eight vision models, three conditions (no legend / 15,000-char text legend / worked examples as images). HEADLINE OBSERVABLE: under the text legend the best model's detected boxes collapsed 94 -> 33 — it became cautious, not accurate. Qwen did not move; image examples were noise. THE FINDING THAT MATTERS: pool every model's answers and between them they see almost everything, but require any two to agree on the same fixture and it collapses — they agree something is there and disagree on WHERE. So the miss is placement and topology, which no detector prompt addresses. STATED CONDITION: single demo plan, type counts rather than pixel-accurate boxes, image-example lever ran once. Confidence MEDIUM, not high.

supporting_research.headline: AECV-Bench corroboration DROPPED 2026-09-20 — compares the same rejected detection-metric class, and both wiki entries carry a spot-verify marker

strategic_opinion.reason: Scheduled Fri 2026-09-25. Best dual-audience post available: a disconfirmed hypothesis published anyway.
strategic_opinion.timing_note: F1 FIGURES REMOVED 2026-09-20 on Seetaram's instruction. F1 on type-multiset detection scores whether the right KINDS and COUNTS of fixtures were found and is blind to WHERE they are — so it can look respectable while the layout is unusable, which for a floor plan is the only thing that matters. The wiki's own consensus finding (pooled recall high, any-two agreement collapses) is the proof. Use raw observables (the 94->33 box collapse) and the placement finding instead. DO NOT reintroduce F1, precision or recall as the deciding parameter for plan-fidelity work in any post.

ideas.title: Our own quality score ranked the worst render first and the shipped one last
ideas.angle: The sharpest engineering-honesty post available. In a paid pilot, the HIGHEST covered_ratio belonged to a render where the model handed the control image back untouched — the worst output of the set. The render the client actually accepted scored LOWEST. Conclusion: the metric is a floor to clear, never a ranking. We measured it, found our own number was wrong, and wrote it down.
ideas.proof_plan: Same control image, same room. Pass-through render covered_ratio 0.7885 (worst image, highest score). Accepted B4 final 0.5216 (shipped image, lowest score). nano-banana-pro round-3 base 0.7527. Whole pilot: 4 renders, ~$0.11 — cost-to-run only, never framed as client savings.

strategic_opinion.reason: Highest-scoring idea in the file and it was never on any plan. Reads to owners as 'they check their own work' and to hiring managers as measurement discipline. Pairs naturally with the contrarian slot.

ideas.title: 'It's not editable' turned out to be three different bugs
ideas.angle: Debugging story with hard before/after numbers. A designer reported fixtures could not be moved. It resolved into two unrelated causes, neither of which was the obvious one: a canvas layer built with listening disabled (so the hit graph was dead), and a calibration that anchored to the image corners assuming the plan bleeds edge to edge. Durable lesson: auto-derived config must announce itself.
ideas.proof_plan: px/ft X 47.82 -> 40.31 (hand-computed truth 40.30). px/ft Y 41.96 -> 40.39 (truth 40.39). Anisotropy 1.1396 -> 0.998 (truth 1.000). Fixtures had been drawn 18.6% too wide and up to ~1.7 ft out of place; one chair box sat outside the building. Test suite 859 -> 871 green. The falsifier fired the same session.

strategic_opinion.reason: The strongest post in the file for the MSc / AI-engineering audience specifically — real debugging, measured against hand-computed truth, with the failure of the fix recorded too. Slightly less legible to a studio owner, so pair it with an owner-facing slot that week.
strategic_opinion.timing_note: created 2026-09-20 from the design-automation wiki (index rebuilt 2026-09-20), never previously ingested

ideas.title: The short prompt filled in the wrong country's emblem
ideas.angle: A condensed prompt made two weak models render real design instead of nothing — and then one of them supplied 'the national emblem' from its own prior: the Chinese state emblem and Chinese officials' portraits, in an Indian government chamber. Whatever a short prompt stops naming, the model invents. So a condensed prompt must keep the culturally and contractually specific nouns.
ideas.proof_plan: ~6,900-char prompt vs an 864-char condensation of the SAME content, same control image, same room. STATED CONDITION: observed on exactly two model families, one room, one control image, one pair of prompt lengths — says nothing about where the breakpoint sits. The wiki explicitly declines to claim a token limit because it could not be confirmed in either vendor's published docs. Keep that hedge.

strategic_opinion.reason: BLOCKED ON PERMISSION, not on proof. The story cannot be told without revealing that the chamber has a national emblem and official portraits. The naming clearance on record covers the firm, the 'government office' description, the floor plan and the render — it explicitly does NOT cover the office's occupant or its emblem/portrait layout. Flagged independently by the drafting agent on 2026-09-20, which refused to use it in the Friday post for the same reason.
strategic_opinion.when_to_post: only if Nine Bricks explicitly clears the emblem/portrait detail in writing
strategic_opinion.timing_note: Unblock condition: written clearance. Alternative: rebuild the post on a non-client prompt-length example, which keeps the lesson and loses the evidence.

ideas.title: Image models have no compass
ideas.angle: Plain-English take with an immediately usable lesson. Telling an image model 'on the south wall at its east end' is unreadable decoration at best and leakage at worst — one model painted the prompt's own room-dimension text onto the ceiling. Placement has to be written viewer-relative. Two separate re-framings turned out to be physically impossible cameras, fixed with zero prompt changes.
ideas.proof_plan: Four models x 3 hard cameras = 12 images, $0.84. One model added a wall-TV, moved a window and painted room-dimension text onto the ceiling. Two re-framings traced to bad auto-cameras (one inside a counter at ~10 deg tilt, one inside a bed footprint). STATED CAVEAT: n=3 cameras, single rolls per model — directional, not a benchmark.

strategic_opinion.reason: Translates a real engineering finding into something a designer can act on tomorrow. Low effort, high clarity, no client dependency.

ideas.title: The 3D editor we decided not to build
ideas.angle: Map-before-build receipt about restraint. Building a full interactive 3D editor to move fixtures looked like the obvious next feature. It would have been the largest build for the least marginal value: plan layout is intrinsically 2D (a point on the floor, a yaw, a footprint) and so is a mouse, so a 3D editor reaches LOWER placement precision than the top-down canvas that already exists.
ideas.proof_plan: Architectural decision with a stated mechanism, not a score. Include the stated limit: it stops holding for genuinely VERTICAL edits (wall-mounted items, hanging lights, ceiling features), where a small 3D height control has unique value a 2D top view cannot express.

strategic_opinion.reason: Deciding NOT to build is the clearest expression of 'map before build', and it is the kind of judgement a hiring manager reads as seniority. No client exposure.

ideas.angle: Build receipt with an unusually honest scope limit. MANDATORY CAVEAT: the segments are BANDS, not a graph, and are DERIVED from the already-corrected model, NOT acquired from a semantic mask. The acquisition bet remains SUSPECT and UNTESTED.

ideas.title: The best tool for the job is often one you cannot use
ideas.angle: Plain-English take on a register we actually keep: approaches that are the best available answer to their sub-problem and remain unusable for a specific named reason — weights withheld, a non-commercial licence, a GPU host we do not have. Tracking the BLOCKER rather than the approach is what lets you re-adopt the moment it lifts. Includes the correction we made to our own register.
ideas.proof_plan: Register entries with named blockers: a visual-primitives model (weights withheld, paper withdrawn); a floor-plan segmentation dataset (CC BY-NC, internal benchmark only); a best-in-class line-lock model (HuggingFace-only, needs a GPU host, infeasible on this machine). Plus the self-correction: two rows were removed on 2026-09-20 because a model rejected on QUALITY is not 'best-but-not-implementable' — it is simply not best.

strategic_opinion.reason: Genuinely useful to any owner evaluating tools, and the self-correction is the interesting half. Slightly abstract, so it needs a concrete week around it rather than leading one.

metric_policy: Added 2026-09-20. For plan-fidelity work, detection scores (F1/precision/recall) and render coverage scores (covered_ratio) are FLOORS TO CLEAR, never rankings, and must never be presented publicly as the parameter that decides whether a model performs. Both have been caught ranking wrongly on this project: covered_ratio scored a pass-through render highest (0.7885) and the client-accepted render lowest (0.5216); detection F1 is blind to placement, which is the only thing a floor plan cares about. Use raw observables and the designer's judgement instead.
